name: Student Result Analyzer
tagline: Upload exam marks as CSV and get validated statistics, grades, missing-data checks and plain-language explanations.
description: A Python data app built with pandas and Streamlit. It validates a CSV of student marks (reporting every problem with its line number), then calculates descriptive statistics for each subject, every student’s percentage, grade, result and rank, the grade distribution and missing scores. Results are explained in plain language and can be downloaded as CSV files and a Markdown report. The analysis code is a separate, fully tested Python package.
features: A fictional sample dataset of 40 students, and a second file with deliberate mistakes to demonstrate validation.
CSV upload with checks for required columns, numeric scores, score range, duplicate or empty IDs, empty names, encoding and malformed rows, each reported with its line number.
Descriptive statistics per subject: count, missing, mean, median, standard deviation, quartiles, minimum, maximum and pass rate.
Student results with total, percentage, grade, Pass/Fail/Incomplete result, rank and subjects below the pass mark.
Grade distribution charts and tables for the whole class and for any single subject.
Missing-value detection per subject and per student, including cells marked AB or Absent.
Plain-language explanations generated from the actual results, plus a glossary of each statistic.
Downloads: student results and subject statistics as CSV, and a Markdown summary report.
limitations: All subjects must share the same maximum marks.
Grades use fixed percentage bands; credit-based GPA or CGPA systems are not implemented.
Only one file is analysed at a time; exams are not compared over time.
Files are limited to 5 MB and 10,000 students.
There is no login; the app only accepts connections from your own computer unless you change its Streamlit settings.
learningObjectives: Load, clean and validate tabular data with pandas.
Compute and interpret descriptive statistics, including how missing values affect them.
Separate analysis logic from the user interface so it can be tested.
Build an interactive data app with Streamlit and Altair charts.
Test data code with pytest and run a Streamlit app headlessly in tests.
ideasForExtension: Allow a different maximum mark for each subject.
Compare two exams and show each student’s improvement.
Export the report as a PDF.
Add correlation analysis between subjects with an explanation of what correlation does and doesn’t show.

prerequisites.name: Python
prerequisites.note: On Windows, tick “Add python.exe to PATH” during installation.

prerequisites.name: A modern web browser
prerequisites.note: Streamlit opens the app in your default browser.

steps.title: Create and activate a virtual environment
steps.note: If PowerShell blocks the activation script, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned once and try again.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.note: Needs an internet connection the first time and downloads roughly 500 MB of packages into .venv.

steps.title: Start the app
steps.note: Streamlit opens http://localhost:8501/ in your browser. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop.

notes: Uploaded files are processed in memory on your own computer and are not saved or sent anywhere.
Change the app name, institution, pass mark and maximum marks in app_config.json, and the accent colour in .streamlit/config.toml.
Activate the virtual environment again each time you open a new terminal.

covers: Every CSV validation rule, including line numbers, encodings, aliases and Unicode names.
Statistics compared with hand-calculated values, grade boundaries, results and ranks.
Missing-value detection and the explanations generated from results.
CSV and Markdown downloads, including formula-injection protection.
A headless run of the Streamlit app with the sample data.

stack.summary: Streamlit runs app.py as a small web server on your own computer and your browser shows the page. The CSV you choose is analysed in memory and nothing is saved; results are downloaded as files.

network.notes: pip install downloads packages once. The app then runs locally; anonymous Streamlit usage statistics are switched off in .streamlit/config.toml.
